# Coding Standards

- All game code must include doc comments on public APIs
- Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in `docs/architecture/`. **How many is
  set by `modes.workflow`** — all ADRs at `full`, *critical* ADRs only at `standard`,
  and none required at `minimal`, where the decision log and `design/game-brief.md`
  carry the rationale instead. See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.
- Gameplay values must be data-driven (external config), never hardcoded
- All public methods must be unit-testable (dependency injection over singletons)
- Commits must reference the relevant design document or task ID
- **Commit messages**: Use Conventional Commits format — `feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`. Reference the story or task ID in the body (e.g., `Story: EPIC-001-S02`).
- **Verification-driven development**: Write tests first when adding gameplay systems.
  For UI changes, verify with screenshots. Compare expected output to actual output
  before marking work complete. Every implementation should have a way to prove it works.
- **A parse check is not a run.** Every story that changes something
  player-observable is launched and observed before it closes, and the
  observation is a retained screenshot in `production/qa/evidence/`. Procedure
  per engine: `.claude/docs/run-and-observe.md`. Not waived at
  `qa.level: minimal` — tests are, the look is not.

# Design Document Standards

- All design docs use Markdown
- Each mechanic has a dedicated document in `design/gdd/`
- **How many of the 8 sections are required depends on `modes.workflow`** —
  all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system defines numeric rules — rates,
  curves, thresholds, costs; the system's `Category` is a hint, not the test) at
  `standard`, and no
  GDD at all at `minimal`, where `design/game-brief.md` is the design record.
  See `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`. The 8 sections:
  1. **Overview** -- one-paragraph summary
  2. **Player Fantasy** -- intended feeling and experience
  3. **Detailed Rules** -- unambiguous mechanics
  4. **Formulas** -- all math defined with variables
  5. **Edge Cases** -- unusual situations handled
  6. **Dependencies** -- other systems listed
  7. **Tuning Knobs** -- configurable values identified
  8. **Acceptance Criteria** -- testable success conditions
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale

# Testing Standards

## Test Evidence by Story Type

All stories must have appropriate test evidence before they can be marked Done:

| Story Type | Required Evidence | Location | Default Gate Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Logic** (formulas, AI, state machines) | Automated unit test — must pass | `tests/unit/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Integration** (multi-system) | Integration test OR documented playtest | `tests/integration/[system]/` | BLOCKING |
| **Visual/Feel** (animation, VFX, feel) | Retained screenshot + lead sign-off | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **UI** (menus, HUD, screens) | Retained screenshot of each screen touched | `production/qa/evidence/` | BLOCKING |
| **Config/Data** (balance tuning) | Smoke check pass | `production/qa/smoke-[date].md` | ADVISORY |

The **Default Gate Level** applies when `testing.strict` is not set in
`project.yaml`. A project may override it per test type: `testing.strict.logic`,
`.integration`, `.visual`, `.ui`, and `.config` each take `true` (BLOCKING) or
`false` (ADVISORY). `/story-done`, `/story-readiness`, `/dev-story`,
`/gate-check`, and `/smoke-check` resolve the effective level from that setting,
falling back to the defaults above when it is absent.

> **Why Visual and UI block.** "Retained" is load-bearing — the screenshot must
> still be on disk in `production/qa/evidence/` when the story is closed. One
> that was captured and discarded is an assertion, not evidence. These two rows
> block because for a game the way it looks *is* the product: an advisory visual
> gate gets deferred in favour of whatever does block, and the result is a
> well-tested game that looks wrong.

> **Exception — `/smoke-check`.** The ADVISORY default for **Config/Data** above
> applies to *per-story evidence* gates. `/smoke-check` is a build-health gate,
> not a per-story evidence gate, so its own unset default for
> `testing.strict.config` is **BLOCKING**. The two defaults differ on purpose.

## Automated Test Rules

- **Naming**: per engine — `.claude/rules/test-standards.md`
- **Determinism**: Tests must produce the same result every run — no random seeds, no time-dependent assertions
- **Isolation**: Each test sets up and tears down its own state; tests must not depend on execution order
- **No hardcoded data**: Test fixtures use constant files or factory functions, not inline magic numbers
  (exception: boundary value tests where the exact number IS the point)
- **Independence**: Unit tests do not call external APIs, databases, or file I/O — use dependency injection

## What NOT to Automate

- Visual fidelity (shader output, VFX appearance, animation curves)
- "Feel" qualities (input responsiveness, perceived weight, timing)
- Platform-specific rendering (test on target hardware, not headlessly)
- Full gameplay sessions (covered by playtesting, not automation)

## CI/CD Rules

- Automated test suite runs on every push to main and every PR
- No merge if tests fail — tests are a blocking gate in CI
- Never disable or skip failing tests to make CI pass — fix the underlying issue
- Engine-specific CI commands:
  - **Godot**: `godot --headless -s -d --remote-debug tcp://127.0.0.1:0 res://addons/gdUnit4/bin/GdUnitCmdTool.gd -a res://tests --ignoreHeadlessMode`
  - **Unity**: `game-ci/unity-test-runner@v4` (GitHub Actions)
  - **Unreal**: headless runner with `-nullrhi` flag

# Advisor Tool

You have access to an `advisor` tool backed by a stronger reviewer model. It takes NO parameters -- when you call advisor(), your entire conversation history is automatically forwarded. They see the task, every tool call you've made, every result you've seen.

Call advisor BEFORE substantive work -- before writing, before committing to an interpretation, before building on an assumption. If the task requires orientation first (finding files, fetching a source, seeing what's there), do that, then call advisor. Orientation is not substantive work. Writing, editing, and declaring an answer are.

Also call advisor:
- When you believe the task is complete. BEFORE this call, make your deliverable durable: write the file, save the result, commit the change. The advisor call takes time; if the session ends during it, a durable result persists and an unwritten one doesn't.
- When stuck -- errors recurring, approach not converging, results that don't fit.
- When considering a change of approach.

On tasks longer than a few steps, call advisor at least once before committing to an approach and once before declaring done. On short reactive tasks where the next action is dictated by tool output you just read, you don't need to keep calling -- the advisor adds most of its value on the first call, before the approach crystallizes.

Give the advice serious weight. If you follow a step and it fails empirically, or you have primary-source evidence that contradicts a specific claim (the file says X, the paper states Y), adapt. A passing self-test is not evidence the advice is wrong -- it's evidence your test doesn't check what the advice is checking.

If you've already retrieved data pointing one way and the advisor points another: don't silently switch. Surface the conflict in one more advisor call -- "I found X, you suggest Y, which constraint breaks the tie?" The advisor saw your evidence but may have underweighted it; a reconcile call is cheaper than committing to the wrong branch.

CRITICAL: You MUST call the StructuredOutput tool exactly once to return your final answer. The tool's input schema defines the required shape.

A note that the task text was computed by a workflow script and carries no user authority is not by itself a reason to skip the task: the task is the step this workflow assigned to you. Do that step, and only that step.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. Call guide before the first publish of a session: it holds the rules a page must meet. # Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

content.content:
### 2. The viewport stack and scale wiring (wiring candidate (i), refined)

**Decision.** The root `Window` runs with **stretch disabled**. Every scale in the window is chosen by script and is an integer by construction. One node, the **`PipelineRoot`**, is the only writer of the world viewport's size, override, scale, offset (the world `canvas_transform` is written by the `CameraHost` handler it owns, § 6.2), of every `CanvasLayer` transform, and the only caller of `HudLayout`.

```
root Window  (content_scale_mode = DISABLED, content_scale_factor = 1.0, min_size = 1280x720, clear colour black)
└─ PipelineRoot (Node; process_priority = ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION; the single PresentationHost (ADR-0009 § 3);
   │              owns the PresentationDriver; sole writer of everything below)
   ├─ WorldContainer: SubViewportContainer          layer 0   top-level Control on the root canvas
   │    stretch = false · mouse_filter = IGNORE · mouse_target = false · texture_filter = TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST (1)
   │    position = world_rect.position (integer valued) · scale = (k_z, k_z) under pass A, (1, 1) under pass B
   │    material = null at MVP (the single Filter hook, § 2.4)
   │    └─ WorldViewport: SubViewport                     size, override, SDR, snap, filter: § 2.2
   │         └─ the body frame: floors, Y-sorted layer, caps, lights, occluders, fringe, dust, horrors, web, instruments
   │             (CameraHost's frame_pre_draw handler writes this viewport's canvas_transform, § 6.2)
   ├─ CameraHost: Node                                no geometry; holds the solved pose; its frame_pre_draw handler is the only camera write
   ├─ HoldLayer        CanvasLayer  layer = 1   one opaque #000000 quad, only in TRANSIT_HOLD and BOOTING / LOADING
   ├─ HudLayer         CanvasLayer  layer = 2   group "hud"; scale = (H, H); offset = hud_rect.position
   │    └─ HudRoot: Control, size = hud_rect.size / H (fractional allowed), Control.scale = (1, 1)
   ├─ MenuPixelLayer   CanvasLayer  layer = 3   scale = (H, H)   bitmap-face chart table and menus
   ├─ MenuReadingLayer CanvasLayer  layer = 4   scale = (1, 1)   reading-face text, sizes in screen px (§ 2.5)
   └─ DebugLayer       CanvasLayer  layer = 5   scale = (H, H)   dev builds only; absent from release exports
```

**2.1 Why this wiring (what the probes show).** Root integer stretch gave exactly `(k, k)` with the correct centring offset at every window tried, but only for the **default step with `H` equal to `k`**: its single scale applies to everything under the root, so a HUD at 3x over a 2x world, or a world at `picture / k_z`, would need a second, non-integer multiplier (the double-scale hazard of PR-7, candidate (ii)). With stretch disabled, a `CanvasLayer.scale` of (3,3) gave a child `Control` an exact scale of 3 with the root transform identity, and a `scale` of (3,3) on a `stretch = false` container gave an exact scale of 3; so the Deck's world 2x and HUD 3x are two independent integers chosen from script. `stretch_shrink` floors (3840/7 gives 548) and is an integer divisor of the container size, so candidate (iii) cannot reach `picture / k_z` at every step and is rejected as the primary; it remains the recorded fallback for the default step only (Alternative 2).

**2.2 The world viewport members the root sets explicitly (every value is the probed built-in default's opposite or must not be inherited).**
- `size`: under pass A `field_px` (the logical size in base px, § 3); under pass B `world_rect.size` (`field_px * k_z`). **Never the 512x512 default and never the window size.** A scene that finds `size == (512, 512)` fails the scene-tree lint.
- `size_2d_override` and `size_2d_override_stretch`: unset (0,0) and `false` under pass A; `field_px` and `true` under pass B. **The override must divide the size exactly** (probed: 1366x768 over 682x384 gives a scale of 2.002933), which § 3 guarantees by sizing the viewport as `field_px * k_z`.
- `use_hdr_2d = false` **at MVP** (the world viewport is SDR like the root). Windowed probe: an HDR viewport drawn through a container on the SDR root outputs unconverted linear colour (a flat `(128, 64, 200)` fill reads back `(55, 13, 147)`; the clear colour `(19, 19, 19)` instead of 76), which contradicts the palette-exact-fills goal, the container-material-null rule (§ 2.4) and `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT, slot = NOT_USED`. The flat-palette guarantee therefore holds only with the world SDR. The HDR path is a specified but unbuilt contingency (§ 2.4), adopted only if lighting spike steps 7 and 8 prove the ambient floor and glow cannot be met without it. Never set on the root viewport.
- `canvas_item_default_texture_filter = Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (0); `use_debanding = false`; `transparent_bg = false`; `handle_input_locally = false` (the world has no `Control`; the effect of this member under a container that forwards no mouse events is UNVERIFIED, step 11, and the member may be left at its default if it proves irrelevant).
- `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel = true`; `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel = true` (belt and braces). **Probed (pass B, Forward+): the flags snap in base-pixel space, not screen-pixel space**, because `canvas_transform` is in override (base-pixel) units; they round to nearest rather than floor. Under pass A the viewport is the base-pixel field, so the same holds. Nothing relies on them: placement is by integer write (ADR-0009), and `pose_q` and the parallax offsets are still written as integer-valued `Vector2` so rounding and flooring never differ. This answers ADR-0009's question on the flags.
- `render_target_update_mode`: `UPDATE_ALWAYS` in `PRESENTING`, `TRANSIT_HOLD` with something to show and `RESCALING`; `UPDATE_DISABLED` in `PAUSED_FROZEN` and `HIDDEN`. **Probed: any size change while the viewport is `UPDATE_DISABLED` clears its target (Forward+ shows `(0, 0, 0)`, Compatibility the clear colour), so `UPDATE_ONCE` set on the frame of any `RESCALING` that happens while updates are disabled is mandatory, not a guard**; it redraws the target and the result is composited the same frame, so it is also sufficient. The engine does not write the mode back after the one-shot (the property still reads `UPDATE_ONCE`), so `PipelineRoot` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` itself on the following frame and **`ViewportWiring` tracks the desired mode in its own field and never reads the property back**. Whether a disabled viewport holds its last texture when no resize occurs (the `PAUSED_FROZEN` hold) is UNVERIFIED but likely; step 11 checks both (pause + resize: no black frame; pause alone: frame held).
- **Nearest filtering is set in three places, with two differently numbered enums**: the project default (`default_texture_filter = 0`), the world viewport member above (`Viewport.DEFAULT_CANVAS_ITEM_TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST`, value 0), and `SubViewportContainer.texture_filter = CanvasItem.TEXTURE_FILTER_NEAREST` (value 1; the probed default is 0 = `PARENT_NODE`, which would inherit and blur the pass-A upscale). Mipmaps are off on every drawn sheet (art bible 8.4). `TileSet.tile_size` is 48x48 and set explicitly on every tile set (checked by ADR-0010's asset and scene lint, § 5.5(b), not at startup).

**2.3 Layers and what is structurally excluded.** The hold plate (1), HUD (2), menus (3 and 4) and debug overlay (5) are `CanvasLayer`s on the **root** viewport; world lights, glow, `CanvasModulate`, the Filter material on the container and the camera transform live in the world viewport or on the container below them and cannot reach them (PR-3, HR-1, HR-6, HR-13). Nothing that must mix with world light may live above layer 0 (it goes in the world); a `Control` found under the world `SubViewport` fails the scene-tree lint, which is a build gate (HUD HS-2). Layers 2 to 5 are **never dimmed, blurred or desaturated** by pause.

**2.4 The single full-screen hook, and the HDR contingency.** The `SubViewportContainer.material` slot is the pipeline's only full-screen hook (PR-10): assigned and nulled **only** by `PipelineRoot.set_filter_material(material: ShaderMaterial)`, colour-writing only (a policy the Filter owns; the pipeline cannot inspect a shader), drawn below every `CanvasLayer`, receiving the world at screen resolution under both passes. **At MVP the slot is null** (the world viewport is SDR, § 2.2) and the pipeline publishes `filter_route = PER_ELEMENT`, `slot = NOT_USED` as a normal state, not an error (TR-pxl-023, TR-percfilter-030). The truth-channel mask route is a VS-A option that this ADR does not pre-build.

**HDR contingency (specified, not built at MVP).** If lighting spike steps 7 and 8 show the ambient floor and glow need a float framebuffer, `use_hdr_2d = true` on the world viewport is adopted by amending this ADR, and the slot then stops being optional: a **mandatory `PipelineRoot`-owned resolve material** (exact linear-to-sRGB per the probed formula in Engine Compatibility, plus a stated clamp or tonemap policy for values above 1.0) is always in the slot. It composes with the Filter **by inclusion**: the Filter's shader includes the same resolve function, so there is one material and one full-screen pass, no second stage; `set_filter_material` refuses a material that lacks the resolve marker while HDR is on. The resolve is **gated on the effective rendering method**: none under Compatibility, which ignores `use_hdr_2d` (the same shader would double-convert, probed `(188, 137, 229)`). Adoption changes `D_filter` to 1 (not 0), makes `filter_route` / `slot` no longer `NOT_USED`, and extends `StartupCheck` with a resolve-present row; the palette read-back test (§ 5.5(d)) then runs against the resolved output on each renderer. Until adoption, `StartupCheck` asserts `use_hdr_2d == false` and `material == null`.

**2.5 Two integer scales and text.** The HUD canvas is `HudRoot`, a `Control` of size `hud_rect.size / H` at the HUD layer's offset; every HUD element anchors to it, `HudLayout` outputs integer HUD-px rectangles relative to it, and `world_to_hud` returns coordinates in its space (PR-12, HUD HS-9). `Control.scale` stays (1,1) on every HUD node and no node animates scale or rotation. **Reading-face text is never drawn under an integer-scaled layer**: the chart table's reading face lives on `MenuReadingLayer` (layer 4, scale (1,1)), whose labels set their font size to `round(base_size * scale_pct * window_scale)` and whose sizes are in screen px, while its pixel-grid face lives on the sibling `MenuPixelLayer` (layer 3, scale `H`). **The two menu layers have distinct indices, so no draw order rests on a tie-break.** (Probed: two same-index siblings draw later-over-earlier, consistent with the sibling index as the sublayer key, which is fragile to reparenting; giving each layer its own index removes the dependency, and the debug layer moves to 5.) The Chart Table's layer budget (`D_L3`) counts both menu layers.

**2.6 One writer, enforced.** Only `PipelineRoot` (and its `ViewportWiring` helper, `src/presentation/pipeline/viewport_wiring.gd`) may write: `SubViewport.size`, `size_2d_override*`, the container's `position`, `scale`, `stretch_shrink` and `material`, any `CanvasLayer.scale` / `offset` / `transform`, `HudRoot.size`; the world viewport's `canvas_transform` and the parallax layer offsets are written only by the **`CameraHost`'s `frame_pre_draw` handler** (§ 6.2). These two are the geometry writers named on ADR-0009's lint allow-list; they are legitimate and do not go through `Placement` (parallax offsets still use `Placement`'s integer helpers). Presentation subscribers (the Filter, Lighting, HUD, Chart Table) call neither; they receive a read-only `RenderLayout` (§ 3) and `world_to_hud`.

### 6. The presentation host, the camera solve and write, and `present_time`

**6.1 The camera is a pure solver run in the `CAMERA_SOLVE` stage (TR-pxl-010, 011, 012, 013, 015; the formulas D.6 to D.10 are the GDD's).** `CameraSolver` is a `RefCounted` with `solve(input: SolverInput, state: SolverState, params: SolverParams) -> Pose`, no scene-tree dependency, float64 per-axis state held as scalars (not `Vector2`), `dt` clamped to `DT_MAX` (0.05 s). The **type of `SolverInput` is the enforcement of Camera C1**: it carries only the follow target's previous and current body-local positions, `tick_alpha`, the raw local beam aim, the zoom step, `dt`, and cut / rebase flags; it has no field through which Attention, breach, horrors, sound, the graph or sanity could enter, so the same input trace gives the same camera trace in calm, tell and breach by construction. The Perception Filter has no write path to a camera or viewport property (§ 2.6). The camera is a `PresenterDescriptor` registered at `PresentationStage.CAMERA_SOLVE` (stage 1, ADR-0009 § 3): it calls `solve` once per frame from `driver.frame` and **publishes `pose_q`, the follow pose `f_q`, the jolt offset, the parallax offsets and the `world_to_hud` inputs** to `CameraHost` and `RenderLayout` before the Avatar, Filter, HUD and Lighting stages run. Solver parameters (`tau_follow`, `DT_MAX`) and `ZOOM_MIN_K` are the `RenderTuning` table loaded by ADR-0007's pipeline and injected (schema in Key Interfaces). Camera state is never persisted.

*Restore and discontinuity.* The kernel calls `snap_baseline` on every interpolated block on each transition into `RUNNING` (ADR-0001 § 4, ADR-0003), so the first frame after a restore interpolates nothing; that is the **only** restore-continuity mechanism and this ADR adds no owner-side rule. The camera stage additionally **CUTs** the solver (starting with `L = 0` easing in) in its `on_discontinuity(DISCONTINUITY_RESTORE)`, which ADR-0009's driver delivers when `PresentationClock.load_seq` changes (the kernel increments it on every `LOADING → RUNNING` transition, restore and new game, never on `PAUSED` or `SAVING → RUNNING`; ADR-0001 amendment batch). A pod or transit body transfer is a CUT; a weld or detach `BODY_TRANSFER` carrying `frame_delta_px` calls `rebase(frame_delta_px)`, which shifts the follow and history and keeps lag and `L`.

**6.2 The frame model and the hook.** `PipelineRoot` **is** ADR-0009's single `PresentationHost` (closing ADR-0009 OQ-E, OQ-J and OQ-L): no other node hosts the driver, and because every step below runs inside one function, no priority tie and no tree-order dependency exists. The composition root constructs the `PresentationDriver` and injects it; `PipelineRoot` holds it. Its single `_process`, at `ProcessPriority.PRESENTATION`, runs in this fixed order: (1) advance `present_time` (§ 6.3); (2) the zoom cooldown (§ 3.1); (3) the `RESCALING` re-derive if dirty (§ 3.2); (4) `driver.frame(delta, present_time)`, which runs the stages with `CAMERA_SOLVE` first. Presenters have no `_process`; **there are no subscribers drawing from their own `_process`** (ADR-0009 Alternatives 1 and 2 reject that shape).

The `CameraHost` (a top-level presentation node under `PipelineRoot`, never a child of a body) connects one handler to **`RenderingServer.frame_pre_draw`**. The handler does exactly two writes from already-solved values and nothing else: the world viewport's `canvas_transform` (from `pose_q` plus the jolt offset) and the parallax layer offsets (integer offsets the camera stage computed with `Placement`'s integer helpers, `floori`, not a bare `-floor(...)`). It **does not solve**, it is **idempotent and branch-free**, and it is **safe if the handler is skipped for a frame** (a minimised or occluded window): the next call writes the then-current solved values and nothing accumulates. **Primary variant: no `Camera2D` in the world tree** (a lint); the transform has scale (1,1), no rotation and no skew every frame and only the host writes it. **Alternative variant**, if the direct write is rejected at step 12: a `Camera2D` with `anchor_mode = ANCHOR_MODE_FIXED_TOP_LEFT` (probed: `anchor_mode` default 1 is `DRAG_CENTER`), drag margins off, and `force_update_scroll()` called after each write; every camera assertion is read as holding on the `Camera2D` if the variant has one. `Camera2D.limit_*` stays at the engine defaults in both variants; **the solver is the only clamp** against the limits rectangle a PROJECTOR sets (ADR-0034), so `world_to_hud` is never offset while `CLAMPED`. A `Camera2D` never descends from a physics body.

*Why the solve is not in the handler.* Probed ordering (windowed 4.7.2 editor, Forward+, main thread, `thread_model` 1 and 2): all node `_process`, then `frame_pre_draw`, then `frame_post_draw`; a `canvas_transform` written in the handler is the one drawn that frame, and a write from `_process` is also drawn that frame. The handler therefore runs after the HUD stage, so a solve inside it would leave `world_to_hud`, the Avatar presenter's beam pose and `mouse_to_world_aim` one frame behind the world: a permanent HUD-versus-world disagreement on exactly the "screen is still when the ship is still" surface (PR-6 C11, TR-pxl-019). Solving in the `_process` pass also keeps the solver unit-testable without a signal that never fires headless.

*Verification status (TD-20).* Windowed 4.7.2 editor: all node `_process`, then `frame_pre_draw`, then `frame_post_draw` (probed); it fires only when a frame is drawn (never headless). Release export, Direct3D 12, the Steam Deck, a minimised or occluded window and `low_processor_mode` are UNVERIFIED (pipeline spike step 12 re-runs the same probe on a release export). `rendering/driver/threads/thread_model` is pinned at 1 (§ 5.1; value 2 unsupported) so the probed ordering holds. **Fallback, used only if `frame_pre_draw` fails the release-export spike:** the canvas write moves to the last statement of `PipelineRoot._process`, after `driver.frame(...)`. That needs no new `ProcessPriority` constant: `PRESENTATION_LATE` is withdrawn (ADR-0001 keeps three constants plus `HOST_SERVICE`).

*Canvas coordinate exactness (TD-23, E14; ADR-0005 TR-shipbody-038 and ADR-0010 cite this paragraph).* **Presentation coordinates are integer-valued `float32` and exact for `|v| <= 2^24` (16,777,216) base px.** `Transform2D`, `Node2D.position` and `Control.position` are `float32` in the standard build (`Engine.is_double_precision()` was not checked and is assumed false). `pose_q` and every placement are `Vector2i`; a `Vector2i` is converted to `Vector2` **only** at `Placement.put` and at the `canvas_transform` write, and the solver's float64 scalars are quantised to `Vector2i` before that conversion, so that conversion is the one point where exactness is kept. World and body-frame extents stay below 2^24 base px; if body-frame extents could exceed that, ADR-0015 owns the bound (the rebase mechanism of § 6.1 exists to keep body-frame coordinates inside it). A unit test constructs the write at `2^24 - 1`, `2^24` and `2^24 + 1` and asserts the first two round-trip and the third is rejected or rebased, never silently rounded.

*Scope edge with ADR-0009.* The Pipeline GDD PR-8 item 3 calls the pipeline root's `frame_pre_draw` handler the "render callback" in which every subscriber reads and draws. That is **not** adopted: subscribers draw from `driver.frame` in the `_process` pass (ADR-0009 § 3), and `frame_pre_draw` is reserved for the `CameraHost`'s two writes. This is returned as a GDD sync item.

**6.3 `present_time`, the pipeline-owned clock (ADR-0001 handed the owner to this ADR).** `PipelineRoot` owns `present_time: float` (seconds, a 64-bit float). Step (1) of `_process` advances it by the `_process` delta while `PresentationClock.state` is `RUNNING`, `SAVING`, or `LOADING` with the hold shown, and leaves it frozen while `PAUSED`; it is **never scaled by reduced motion** (reduced motion scales individual effects). Layer 0 animation uses only `present_time` (delivered to presenters as `PresentFrame.present_time`); the menu layers (3 and 4) and the debug layer (5) run on engine process time so the chart table responds while paused; the HUD (layer 2) freezes with the world. The cosmetic-phase rule ("the tick counter is never used for cosmetic phase") is ADR-0001's and is not restated. The kernel state comes from the read-only `PresentationClock.state: int` (the kernel state enum: `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `SAVING`, `LOADING`, `FAULTED`), and `setup()` takes `PresentationClock` only; no `KernelStateView` type exists. This depends on the ADR-0001 amendment batch (Depends On, Ordering Note). `SceneTree.paused` is not the kernel's pause and is not used by the pipeline.

**6.4 Pipeline states.** The pipeline state machine (`BOOTING`, `PRESENTING`, `RESCALING`, `TRANSIT_HOLD`, `PAUSED_FROZEN`, `HIDDEN`, with the `DEBUG_OVERLAY` modifier) is implemented as the GDD's States and Transitions table, with the camera state as three independent fields (follow, zoom, hold). The wiring-specific rules recorded here: `PAUSED_FROZEN` sets `UPDATE_DISABLED` and holds an undimmed last frame (a resize while paused forces the one-shot `UPDATE_ONCE` of § 2.2, or the held frame would be blank); `TRANSIT_HOLD` shows the layer-1 black quad (`#000000`, no text) with a 120 ms fade in and a cut out; `FAULTED` is not a pipeline state (the pipeline keeps presenting the last committed state; a dev build halts with the overlay); any `(state, trigger)` pair not listed is ignored and reported to diagnostics.

### 7. The draw-call and timing budget rules (architecture IC-6)

The Pipeline GDD owns the frame budget (D.16 and the Performance block) and therefore the **figures**; this ADR owns the **rules**: one table, draw calls read **per viewport**, an owner column, and withholding a zoom step rather than cutting content. The table below mirrors the GDD's D.16 as of 2026-10-28 so the nesting is visible in one place. **A system raises its row by amending the GDD's D.16 block (then this mirror is refreshed); this Foundation ADR is amended only if a rule changes, not after each spike measurement or system budget change.** Every figure is a proposal pending release-export measurement on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK (recorded with the printed renderer and driver); until measured, a performance criterion is neither a pass nor a fail. Draw calls are read per viewport with `Viewport.get_render_info(Viewport.RENDER_INFO_TYPE_CANVAS, Viewport.RENDER_INFO_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME)` (enums probed: type 2, info 2; 0 headless; works per viewport in Forward+ and Compatibility, probed) so the HUD's number is never confused with the sorted layer's. `DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME` is read after the frame, so a value read in `_process` **lags one frame**. **Probed: the container composite is counted on the root, one call per `SubViewportContainer`** (a root with only three containers reported 3), so the table carries it as its own row.

**7.1 Draw calls (default field and every zoom-in step).**

**7.2 Zoom-out steps.** The single `D_world <= 350` cap cannot hold when 4x to 9x the content is in view (D.16 arithmetic). At every zoom-out step (the Deck's 1280x800 field, 1080p at 1x, the bottom steps of 1440p and 2160p) only `D_world + D_root <= 1000` applies, **plus** the P99 total-frame ceilings below. A step that cannot meet both on RM-DESKTOP or RM-DECK is **withheld** (static table `ZOOM_MIN_K`, set from the measured table and never changed by a live measurement), never "fixed" by cutting content (default D5, confirmed by ruling R20). **5.2 The `RenderConfigSnapshot` and `StartupCheck` (pure).** The startup assertion reads the effective values into one value object, `RenderConfigSnapshot`, built by `RenderConfigReader` (the only code that calls `ProjectSettings`, `RenderingServer` and the viewport getters for this purpose), and `StartupCheck.run(snapshot, expected) -> Array[StartupFinding]` is a pure function over it. **The reader uses explicit typed assignments**, never inference and never `as`: `var v: int = ProjectSettings.get_setting(&"...")` (the cast pattern ADR-0010 `PRJ-02` states once), because ADR-0010 makes inferred and unsafe declarations errors. A `StartupFinding` is a value `{code: StringName, key: String, expected: String, actual: String}`; there is no `assert`, `push_error` or `quit` in the check. The pipeline root (dev build) halts before any window is presented when the array is non-empty and prints the table. A release build treats a **method or driver finding as fatal** (the visible "unsupported GPU" screen of § 1, plus the diagnostics header) and writes every other finding to the diagnostics header and continues. Doctored snapshots exercise every finding in gdUnit4 with no window. **Startup findings are pipeline-local values written to the diagnostics header; they are not kernel faults, there is no fault domain for them at MVP (the pipeline root builds in BOOTING step 2, before the kern

When `DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless"` the **live** `RenderingServer` method and driver rows are reported **NOT ASSESSED** (probed: a headless run reports `gl_compatibility`), never as a mismatch and never as a pass. **CI does not need the live rows:** `ProjectSettings.get_setting` of `rendering_method`, `driver.windows` and `driver.linuxbsd` returns the effective configured value headless, independent of the live headless `opengl3` driver, and CI asserts those (the driver keys are default-equal and therefore absent from `project

**5.4 The scale readback chain (the acceptance criterion is pinned here because the GDD wording measures different things in A and B).** `get_final_transform()` of the world `SubViewport` is identity under pass A (the multiplication lives in the container) and the stretch scale under pass B. The criterion `get_final_transform().get_scale() == (k, k)` is therefore replaced by one chain that is mode-independent:
- **World effective scale** = `root.get_final_transform().get_scale()` (identity, stretch disabled) x `WorldContainer.get_global_transform().get_scale()` x `WorldViewport.get_stretch_transform().get_scale()`, asserted exactly `(k_z, k_z)` (integer comparison on `Vector2` components that are integer-valued by construction; no epsilon).
- **HUD effective scale** = `root.get_final_transform().get_scale()` x `HudLayer.transform.get_scale()` (and `Control.get_global_transform_with_canvas().get_scale()` of a probe `Control` under it), asserted exactly `(H, H)`.
`ViewportWiring.read_back() -> WiringReadback` returns these, and the same readback table is logged at boot.

**5.5 CI, lints and the tree walk (TR-pxl-028).** (a) **One headless gdUnit4 test with two read tiers** (it is ADR-0010 `PRJ-02`; this section's table is its normative key list, including the `fallback_to_*` keys and `thread_model`). Rows marked **required** are checked for presence and value with `ConfigFile`; rows marked **absent is correct**, including `physics/common/physics_interpolation` (absent or false) and the renderer and driver keys, are checked with `ProjectSettings.get_setting` effective values, because a `ConfigFile` read cannot see an absent key's effective default. `ConfigFile` structural checks (an empty `[autoload]`) stay at ADR-0010's E2 tier. The test fails naming exactly the offending key when a fixture copy has one key removed or set wrong, one key per run. (b) The scene-tree and asset lint (ADR-0010 chooses the tool and which rules are regex or boot walk): no `Camera2D` descends from a `PhysicsBody2D`; no `Control` and no node in group `hud` under the world viewport; `rotation == 0` on every node under the environment, pipe, prop, actor and HUD groups; `Control.scale == (1,1)` on every HUD node; **every loaded `TileSet.tile_size == (48, 48)` and none `(16, 16)`**; no `SubViewport.size == (512,512)`; a scan for assignments to `Camera2D.zoom`; the layer indices of § 2 are distinct. (c) A debug-only per-frame tree walk behind a console toggle flags fraction

The player-facing render options are an enumerated set only: world scale Auto or an integer of at least 2 from the offered list, HUD scale an integer in `[H_default, 2 * H_default]` (3 to 6 at 1080p), frame cap and V-sync mode (enabled, mailbox, off; no adaptive), and the reading-face scale (80 to 200 percent, the one continuous control), persisted by the same host-local `SettingsStore` (ADR-0030). No gamma, brightness, contrast, sharpening or filter option exists, and `apply_display_settings` rejects any `aspect`, `manual_k` or `hud_scale` value outside the offered enumeration (Pipeline GDD PR-14, TR-pxl-033).
